reason: The text depicts Yahweh as the God of the nation Israel throughout. Key evidence includes: (1) Yahweh explicitly redeems and guides 'this people' (עַם־ז֣וּ) whom he has chosen; (2) Yahweh is portrayed as 'a man of war' fighting on Israel's behalf, destroying Pharaoh's army for Israel's deliverance; (3) Yahweh leads Israel to 'the habitation of your holiness' (your sanctuary); (4) Israel is described as people whom Yahweh has 'acquired' or 'purchased' (קָנִֽיתָ); (5) Yahweh will plant Israel in 'the mountain of your inheritance' (הַ֣ר נַחֲלָֽתְךָ֔), establishing Israel as a nation in their own land; (6) Yahweh will 'reign forever and ever' (יִמְלֹ֖ךְ לְעֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד) as Israel's eternal king. The entire song celebrates Yahweh's specific covenant relationship with Israel as a nation, characterized by military protection, divine guidance, and territorial establishment.
